subject: health
title: Correction and reflection: emergency versus non-emergency support
essentialQuestion: How can understanding whole-person wellbeing and trusted support help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool
keyPoints: An emergency involves immediate danger or a person who may be seriously hurt or unable to respond; non-emergency concerns still deserve timely support through a trusted adult or professional.
Classify urgency from observable facts, protect scene safety, activate trained help, and stay within current training rather than attempting an unsafe rescue.
For emergency versus non-emergency support, a strong response distinguishes fact from assumption, uses a fictional or public case, and includes a safe next step or appropriate source of support.
privacySafeScenario: Create a private-safe support map and a reliable-information checklist.
studentTask: Read three supplied fictional situations about emergency versus non-emergency support. For each, mark routine, urgent, or emergency; list the first safe action, the trained help to contact, and one action a bystander should avoid. Support each classification with a fact from the lesson.
knowledgeCheck: In two or three sentences, explain the most important distinction in emergency versus non-emergency support; use one lesson fact and name the evidence, safety check, or support route that makes the explanation dependable.
completionCriteria: The response completes every named part of the emergency versus non-emergency support task using the supplied fictional or public case.
The response uses at least two accurate details from the lesson instruction and distinguishes evidence from assumption.
The response gives a safe, feasible next step or support route and does not depend on private disclosure, body comparison, or recorded media proof.
